system.description:
Not every ranger works alone. Some build a partnership with the wild, starting with whatever creature will have them, and in time earning the trust of things that shouldn't trust anyone.

  • Reshapes: adds a companion to your Hunter's Tricks and Marked Prey.
  • Bonded Companion (1st): tame and bond with a beast companion that fights and travels with you: at 1st level a mundane animal suited to the terrain (wolf, hawk, boar), bonded over a few days of feeding and handling.
    • Its Level is half your Ranger level (rounded up), and ½ at 1st and 2nd level: use the block of an animal of that Level or lower, or the HP, AC, attack and damage targets for that Level in Monsters & Treasure.
    • It acts straight after your turn, and you control it fully (where it moves, what it attacks and what it does), at no cost to your own action.
    • It is not a summoned attacker (see Spellcasting in Arneyan).
    • If it is slain, a replacement of a Level you could bond can be found after one Downtime Phase of searching.
  • Beastspeaker (1st): Advantage on checks to calm, speak with or avoid provoking wild animals and bestial or animal-like monsters, even ones far beyond what you could safely fight. You can calm a creature this way, but you can't control or tame it unless it is bonded to you.
  • Wild Bond (5th): you may try to tame a bestial or animal-like monster of low power, at the GM's discretion, in place of your animal: it uses its own block, and its Level can be no higher than half your Ranger level (rounded up), such as a dire wolf at 5th or a giant spider from 7th. Taming takes days of exposure and a Wisdom check the GM sets by the creature's Level and temper, and can fail or provoke an attack.
  • Apex Bond (9th): you may try the same with a dangerous bestial or animal-like monster, at the GM's discretion, under the same Level limit (a winter wolf at 10th, a manticore or griffon from 13th, a wyvern from 17th); failure is likely to mean a fight.
